claims.title: Legendary founding of Van Lang
claims.summary: Vietnamese tradition dates the kingdom of Van Lang and its line of Hung kings to 2879 BCE; the historical Bronze Age Dong Son culture of the Red River delta flourished in the first millennium BCE.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vietnam: A thousand years under Chinese rule, a thousand more of fiercely defended independence, and a modern nation forged in war and reform.", terralore.co/country/VNM/chronicle#ev-2879bce-legendary-founding-of-van-lang, claim TL:VNM:event:2879bce:legendary-founding-of-van-lang, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Kingdom of Au Lac and Co Loa
claims.summary: An Duong Vuong overthrows the last Hung king and unites the land as Au Lac, building the fortified capital of Co Loa north of modern Hanoi.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vietnam: A thousand years under Chinese rule, a thousand more of fiercely defended independence, and a modern nation forged in war and reform.", terralore.co/country/VNM/chronicle#ev-257bce-kingdom-of-au-lac-and-co-loa, claim TL:VNM:event:257bce:kingdom-of-au-lac-and-co-loa, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Han conquest begins Chinese rule
claims.summary: The Chinese Han dynasty conquers the region, opening more than a thousand years of direct Chinese administration, taxation, and cultural influence.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vietnam: A thousand years under Chinese rule, a thousand more of fiercely defended independence, and a modern nation forged in war and reform.", terralore.co/country/VNM/chronicle#ev-111bce-han-conquest-begins-chinese-rule, claim TL:VNM:event:111bce:han-conquest-begins-chinese-rule, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Revolt of the Trung sisters
claims.summary: Trung Trac and Trung Nhi lead a rebellion that briefly drives out the Chinese before being defeated in 43 CE; they become lasting symbols of Vietnamese resistance.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vietnam: A thousand years under Chinese rule, a thousand more of fiercely defended independence, and a modern nation forged in war and reform.", terralore.co/country/VNM/chronicle#ev-40-revolt-of-the-trung-sisters, claim TL:VNM:event:40:revolt-of-the-trung-sisters, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Battle of Bach Dang and independence
claims.summary: Ngo Quyen destroys a Southern Han fleet at the Bach Dang River using hidden iron-tipped stakes, ending Chinese rule; he proclaims himself king in 939.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vietnam: A thousand years under Chinese rule, a thousand more of fiercely defended independence, and a modern nation forged in war and reform.", terralore.co/country/VNM/chronicle#ev-938-battle-of-bach-dang-and-independence, claim TL:VNM:event:938:battle-of-bach-dang-and-independence, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of the Ly dynasty
claims.summary: Ly Cong Uan takes the throne and founds the Ly dynasty, moving the capital to Thang Long (Hanoi) in 1010 and establishing the enduring institutions of independent Dai Viet.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vietnam: A thousand years under Chinese rule, a thousand more of fiercely defended independence, and a modern nation forged in war and reform.", terralore.co/country/VNM/chronicle#ev-1009-founding-of-the-ly-dynasty, claim TL:VNM:event:1009:founding-of-the-ly-dynasty, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Tran defeat of the Mongol invasions
claims.summary: Under Tran Hung Dao the Tran dynasty repels three invasions by Kublai Khan's Mongols, climaxing in the 1288 victory at the Bach Dang River where the Mongol fleet is destroyed on hidden stakes.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vietnam: A thousand years under Chinese rule, a thousand more of fiercely defended independence, and a modern nation forged in war and reform.", terralore.co/country/VNM/chronicle#ev-1258-tran-defeat-of-the-mongol-invasions, claim TL:VNM:event:1258:tran-defeat-of-the-mongol-invasions, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ming China occupies Dai Viet
claims.summary: The Chinese Ming dynasty conquers Dai Viet and imposes two decades of harsh direct rule, provoking widespread resistance.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vietnam: A thousand years under Chinese rule, a thousand more of fiercely defended independence, and a modern nation forged in war and reform.", terralore.co/country/VNM/chronicle#ev-1407-ming-china-occupies-dai-viet, claim TL:VNM:event:1407:ming-china-occupies-dai-viet, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Le Loi expels the Ming and founds the Le dynasty
claims.summary: After a ten-year war of liberation, Le Loi drives out the Ming, restores independence, and establishes the Le dynasty, which would rule, nominally, for centuries.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vietnam: A thousand years under Chinese rule, a thousand more of fiercely defended independence, and a modern nation forged in war and reform.", terralore.co/country/VNM/chronicle#ev-1428-le-loi-expels-the-ming-and-founds-the-le-dynasty, claim TL:VNM:event:1428:le-loi-expels-the-ming-and-founds-the-le-dynasty, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Conquest of Champa's capital
claims.summary: Emperor Le Thanh Tong's forces capture Vijaya, the capital of Champa, accelerating the southward expansion (Nam tien) of Vietnamese settlement.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vietnam: A thousand years under Chinese rule, a thousand more of fiercely defended independence, and a modern nation forged in war and reform.", terralore.co/country/VNM/chronicle#ev-1471-conquest-of-champa-s-capital, claim TL:VNM:event:1471:conquest-of-champa-s-capital, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Tay Son rebellion
claims.summary: A peasant-led uprising overthrows the Nguyen and Trinh lords and the Le dynasty, and in 1789 routs an invading Chinese Qing army near Thang Long.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vietnam: A thousand years under Chinese rule, a thousand more of fiercely defended independence, and a modern nation forged in war and reform.", terralore.co/country/VNM/chronicle#ev-1771-tay-son-rebellion, claim TL:VNM:event:1771:tay-son-rebellion, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Gia Long founds the Nguyen dynasty
claims.summary: Nguyen Anh defeats the Tay Son, reunifies the country, and is crowned emperor as Gia Long at Hue, founding Vietnam's last imperial dynasty.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vietnam: A thousand years under Chinese rule, a thousand more of fiercely defended independence, and a modern nation forged in war and reform.", terralore.co/country/VNM/chronicle#ev-1802-gia-long-founds-the-nguyen-dynasty, claim TL:VNM:event:1802:gia-long-founds-the-nguyen-dynasty, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The name Vietnam adopted
claims.summary: The unified realm is recognized under the name Vietnam, with its capital at Hue and a centralized administration modeled on Qing China.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vietnam: A thousand years under Chinese rule, a thousand more of fiercely defended independence, and a modern nation forged in war and reform.", terralore.co/country/VNM/chronicle#ev-1804-the-name-vietnam-adopted, claim TL:VNM:event:1804:the-name-vietnam-adopted, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Reign of Minh Mang
claims.summary: Emperor Minh Mang consolidates the Confucian state, completes administrative reforms, and intensifies suspicion of European traders and Catholic missionaries.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vietnam: A thousand years under Chinese rule, a thousand more of fiercely defended independence, and a modern nation forged in war and reform.", terralore.co/country/VNM/chronicle#ev-1820-reign-of-minh-mang, claim TL:VNM:event:1820:reign-of-minh-mang, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: French attack on Da Nang
claims.summary: A French and Spanish naval force assaults Da Nang, beginning the military conquest that would bring Vietnam under colonial rule.

sources.label: Vietnam: A Country Study
sources.publisher: U.S. Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.title: France annexes Cochinchina
claims.summary: Following the capture of Saigon, France secures the southern provinces of Cochinchina as a colony, its first permanent foothold in Vietnam.

sources.label: Vietnam: A Country Study
sources.publisher: U.S. Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vietnam: A thousand years under Chinese rule, a thousand more of fiercely defended independence, and a modern nation forged in war and reform.", terralore.co/country/VNM/chronicle#ev-1862-france-annexes-cochinchina, claim TL:VNM:event:1862:france-annexes-cochinchina, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: French Indochina established
claims.summary: France unites Cochinchina, Annam, Tonkin, and Cambodia into the Indochinese Union; Laos is added in 1893, binding Vietnam into a colonial federation centered on Hanoi.

sources.label: Vietnam: A Country Study
sources.publisher: U.S. Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vietnam: A thousand years under Chinese rule, a thousand more of fiercely defended independence, and a modern nation forged in war and reform.", terralore.co/country/VNM/chronicle#ev-1887-french-indochina-established, claim TL:VNM:event:1887:french-indochina-established, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of the Indochinese Communist Party
claims.summary: Ho Chi Minh helps unite rival communist groups into the Indochinese Communist Party, which becomes the organizational core of the independence struggle.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vietnam: A thousand years under Chinese rule, a thousand more of fiercely defended independence, and a modern nation forged in war and reform.", terralore.co/country/VNM/chronicle#ev-1930-founding-of-the-indochinese-communist-party, claim TL:VNM:event:1930:founding-of-the-indochinese-communist-party, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Great Vietnamese Famine
claims.summary: Under Japanese occupation and wartime mismanagement, famine strikes northern Vietnam, killing an estimated one to two million people and deepening revolutionary discontent.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vietnam: A thousand years under Chinese rule, a thousand more of fiercely defended independence, and a modern nation forged in war and reform.", terralore.co/country/VNM/chronicle#ev-1945-great-vietnamese-famine, claim TL:VNM:event:1945:great-vietnamese-famine, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Declaration of independence
claims.summary: As Japan surrenders, the Viet Minh seize power in the August Revolution and Ho Chi Minh proclaims the Democratic Republic of Vietnam in Hanoi's Ba Dinh Square.

sources.label: Proclamation of Independence of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam (1945)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vietnam: A thousand years under Chinese rule, a thousand more of fiercely defended independence, and a modern nation forged in war and reform.", terralore.co/country/VNM/chronicle#ev-1945-declaration-of-independence, claim TL:VNM:event:1945:declaration-of-independence, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First Indochina War
claims.summary: War between France and the Viet Minh ends with the French defeat at Dien Bien Phu on 7 May 1954, terminating French colonial rule in Vietnam.

sources.label: Dien Bien Phu and the Fall of French Indochina, 1954
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vietnam: A thousand years under Chinese rule, a thousand more of fiercely defended independence, and a modern nation forged in war and reform.", terralore.co/country/VNM/chronicle#ev-1946-first-indochina-war, claim TL:VNM:event:1946:first-indochina-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Geneva Accords divide Vietnam
claims.summary: The Geneva Conference partitions Vietnam at the 17th parallel into a communist North and an anti-communist South pending reunification elections that are never held.

sources.label: Dien Bien Phu and the Fall of French Indochina, 1954
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.title: Gulf of Tonkin and U.S. escalation
claims.summary: The Gulf of Tonkin incident leads Congress to pass a resolution authorizing the vast escalation of direct U.S. military involvement in the war.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vietnam: A thousand years under Chinese rule, a thousand more of fiercely defended independence, and a modern nation forged in war and reform.", terralore.co/country/VNM/chronicle#ev-1964-gulf-of-tonkin-and-u-s-escalation, claim TL:VNM:event:1964:gulf-of-tonkin-and-u-s-escalation, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Tet Offensive
claims.summary: A coordinated communist surprise offensive across South Vietnam, though costly militarily, undermines American public support and shifts the war toward U.S. withdrawal.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vietnam: A thousand years under Chinese rule, a thousand more of fiercely defended independence, and a modern nation forged in war and reform.", terralore.co/country/VNM/chronicle#ev-1968-tet-offensive, claim TL:VNM:event:1968:tet-offensive, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Fall of Saigon and reunification
claims.summary: North Vietnamese forces capture Saigon, ending the war; the country is formally reunified as the Socialist Republic of Vietnam on 2 July 1976.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vietnam: A thousand years under Chinese rule, a thousand more of fiercely defended independence, and a modern nation forged in war and reform.", terralore.co/country/VNM/chronicle#ev-1975-fall-of-saigon-and-reunification, claim TL:VNM:event:1975:fall-of-saigon-and-reunification, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Sino-Vietnamese War
claims.summary: China invades northern Vietnam in response to Vietnam's ousting of the Khmer Rouge in Cambodia; the brief but bloody border war deepens Vietnam's isolation.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vietnam: A thousand years under Chinese rule, a thousand more of fiercely defended independence, and a modern nation forged in war and reform.", terralore.co/country/VNM/chronicle#ev-1979-sino-vietnamese-war, claim TL:VNM:event:1979:sino-vietnamese-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Doi Moi reforms launched
claims.summary: The Communist Party's Sixth Congress adopts Doi Moi, replacing central planning with a socialist-oriented market economy and opening Vietnam to private enterprise and foreign investment.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vietnam: A thousand years under Chinese rule, a thousand more of fiercely defended independence, and a modern nation forged in war and reform.", terralore.co/country/VNM/chronicle#ev-1986-doi-moi-reforms-launched, claim TL:VNM:event:1986:doi-moi-reforms-launched, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Normalization with the U.S. and ASEAN membership
claims.summary: Vietnam restores diplomatic relations with the United States and joins the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, ending decades of isolation.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vietnam: A thousand years under Chinese rule, a thousand more of fiercely defended independence, and a modern nation forged in war and reform.", terralore.co/country/VNM/chronicle#ev-1995-normalization-with-the-u-s-and-asean-membership, claim TL:VNM:event:1995:normalization-with-the-u-s-and-asean-membership, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Accession to the World Trade Organization
claims.summary: Vietnam joins the WTO, cementing its integration into the global economy and accelerating an export-driven manufacturing boom.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vietnam: A thousand years under Chinese rule, a thousand more of fiercely defended independence, and a modern nation forged in war and reform.", terralore.co/country/VNM/chronicle#ev-2007-accession-to-the-world-trade-organization, claim TL:VNM:event:2007:accession-to-the-world-trade-organization, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
